sample_unit: readings (6 radiologists x 40 imaging studies per session)

links.outcome: Radiologist diagnostic accuracy and confidence with vs without GPT-4 assistance
links.effect: Top-3 diagnostic accuracy improved from 181/240 (75.4%) unassisted to 188/240 (78.3%) AI-assisted; diagnostic confidence significantly higher with AI assistance.
links.quote: When assessing if the correct diagnosis was among the top-3 differential diagnoses, diagnostic accuracy improved slightly from 181/240 (75.4%, unassisted) to 188/240 (78.3%, AI-assisted).

links.outcome: Rate of hallucinations and misinterpretations in GPT-4 responses
links.effect: 23 responses (7.4%) classified as hallucinations and 2 (0.6%) as misinterpretations among 309 prompts.
links.quote: Twenty-three responses (7.4%) were classified as hallucinations, while two (0.6%) were misinterpretations.

screen.reason: This empirical reader study compares radiologists' diagnostic accuracy, confidence, and workflow with versus without GPT-4 assistance, evaluating human-in-the-loop AI assistance and measuring hallucination rates.
